ranking_by: volume of the pyramid in cubic metres
subject: ancient pyramid
title: The 5 Biggest Pyramids on Earth, Ranked (The Great Pyramid Is Only #2)

scenes.text: The five biggest pyramids ever built, by volume. The Great Pyramid of Giza doesn't win.

scenes.label: Bent Pyramid · 1.24M m³
scenes.text: Number five: the Bent Pyramid of Dahshur, Egypt. About 1.24 million cubic metres, with a kink where the builders changed the angle mid-job.

scenes.label: Red Pyramid · 1.69M m³
scenes.text: Number four: the Red Pyramid, next door at Dahshur. Around 1.69 million cubic metres, 105 metres tall, built for the pharaoh Sneferu.

scenes.label: Pyramid of Khafre · 2.2M m³
scenes.text: Number three: the Pyramid of Khafre at Giza. About 2.2 million cubic metres, with the Sphinx at its feet.

scenes.label: Great Pyramid · 2.5M m³
scenes.text: Number two: the Great Pyramid of Giza. Roughly 2.5 million cubic metres and 146 metres tall when finished.

scenes.label: Cholula · 4.45M m³
scenes.text: Number one: the Great Pyramid of Cholula, Mexico. About 4.45 million cubic metres, nearly twice Giza. Today it looks like a hill, with a church on top.

description:
The five biggest pyramids on Earth, ranked by volume. The Great Pyramid of Cholula in Mexico, about 4.45 million cubic metres, is the largest pyramid ever built; it now looks like a hill with a Spanish church on top.
The Great Pyramid of Giza (about 2.5 million cubic metres), the Pyramid of Khafre (2.2 million), the Red Pyramid (1.69 million) and the Bent Pyramid (1.24 million) complete the list.
Did you know the biggest pyramid is in Mexico?
first_comment: Cholula was built up in stages from the 3rd century BC to the 9th century AD and was abandoned before the Spanish arrived. Which would you put at number one, and what should we rank next?
